evidence.note: Reads the official /app/evaluate.py to understand how binary_strict is computed before trusting numbers.
Investigates the llama3 renderer, traces renderer usage in the evaluator, and writes eval_llama3.py to ensure the required Llama 3 chat renderer is used for the metric.
Reproduces the base-model baseline, including a dedicated 'Baseline llama3 eval' that validates the harness reproduces the ~26% target regime with the correct renderer.
Runs the OFFICIAL evaluator on the best checkpoint and confirms the best_checkpoint file — an independent check that the claimed number matches the spec metric, not just the custom fast eval.
Re-verifies top candidate checkpoints with repeated and 3rd evals, reproducing scores and implicitly confirming each recorded best checkpoint is loadable/samplable.
No explicit guard against IFEval leakage/paraphrase contamination or held-out generalization sanity check appears anywhere in the trajectory.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it reproduces the baseline with the correct renderer (step 105), verifies binary_strict against spec by running the official evaluator on the best checkpoint (step 255), and repeatedly re-evaluates top candidates to confirm reproducibility and that checkpoints load/sample (steps 332-338, 370-377). It falls short of anchor 8/10 because there is no explicit sanity-check that gains come from legitimate (non-leaked) data and no held-out overfitting/memorization test. This places the observed behavior at a 7 — strong instrumentation of the eval and checkpoint reproducibility, but missing the explicit leakage/generalization reasoning.
